text: I see you are experiencing jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any abdominal pain, particularly in the right upper quadrant?

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of diabetes mellitus, or have you experienced any unintentional weight loss prior to these recent symptoms? I also need to know if you have noticed any fever or chills, which might suggest an infectious cause like cholangitis.

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of pancreatitis and significant smoking, I suspect a malignancy in the head of the pancreas obstructing the bile duct. REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen_Pelvis_With_Contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan was normal, I need to rule out other causes of obstructive jaundice, such as cholangiocarcinoma or primary sclerosing cholangitis. Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or greasy, foul-smelling stools?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Episode of acute upper abdominal pain treated three years ago. History of long-term alcohol consumption and smoking. Social history: Stopped alcohol consumption three years ago; 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of pancreatitis, significant smoking, and obstructive jaundice with a normal CT, I suspect an intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm or cholangiocarcinoma that may have been missed. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP demonstrates marked dilation of the common bile duct and intrahepatic bile ducts. A filling defect is noted in the distal common bile duct, suggestive of a stricture or mass. No definite pancreatic mass is visualized, but the ductal dilation is significant.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRCP shows a filling defect in the distal common bile duct, which explains your obstructive jaundice. To determine if this is a benign stricture or a malignancy like cholangiocarcinoma, I need to visualize the duct directly and obtain tissue samples. REQUEST TEST: ERCP_with_biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ERCP reveals a stricture in the distal common bile duct. Brush cytology and biopsy of the stricture show atypical glandular cells consistent with cholangiocarcinoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms cholangiocarcinoma, a cancer of the bile ducts. I will now coordinate with surgical oncology to discuss potential resection options and palliative care strategies. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cholangiocarcinoma
